## 1500 W Wilson Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN:** 14171060250000 | **Parcel resolution:** authoritative (county address records)
*Municipal Code current through the Council Journal of March 18, 2026; a later amendment may not be reflected.*

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2 (Neighborhood Shopping, dash-2 density)** per the City's official GIS zoning layer, last updated 2025-03-19. No rezoning ordinance is on record — the district has not been recently changed. Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Residential Use — Above Ground Floor & Ground Floor

- **Residential above ground floor: Yes.** The B1 district permits residential dwelling units on or above the ground floor [1]. Mixed-use (retail below, apartments above) is the intended form.
- **Ground-floor residential: Not by right for new residential.** [1] specifies that B1 is intended for small-scale retail and services at ground level; residential is permitted *on or above* the ground floor, meaning a purely residential ground floor is not the standard permitted use. However, [4] (§17-3-0400) contains an exception allowing the Zoning Administrator to approve conversion of an occupied or vacant ground-floor commercial space in a multi-story building into dwelling units under §17-13-1003-NN — but this is an administrative approval, not a by-right permit.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

From the zoning table for B1-2 [1] (§17-3-0102):

| Standard | B1-2 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 2.2 |
| **Max Height** | 45–50 ft (varies by lot frontage & ground-floor commercial) |
| **Min Lot Area per Dwelling Unit** | 1,000 sq ft |
| **Lot Coverage** | Not specified in retrieved data |
| **Setbacks** | Not specified in retrieved data |

**Unit yield by lot area:** This parcel's lot is 4,347 sq ft ÷ 1,000 sq ft/unit = **up to 4 units by lot-area math alone.** This is a lot-area ceiling only — FAR, height, parking, and other standards may reduce the actual buildable count; efficiency or SRO units counted at smaller areas could allow more [4].

Verify setbacks and lot coverage at §17-3-0500 of the Municipal Code (not in the retrieved text).

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **No Planned Development.** No PD applies.
- **No landmark or historic district.** Not a landmark building, not in a landmark or historic district, not on the National Register.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA & Metra).** Both a CTA-TOD and Metra-TOD overlay apply. The nearest CTA rail is Montrose (Brown Line), 0.45 mi away; the nearest Metra station is Ravenswood (Union Pacific North), 0.39 mi away.
- **ADU-Allowed Area — Zone 1** [3] (§17-7-0573, §17-7-0574). No limitations apply in this zone. Coach houses and conversion units are also permitted by right in this B1 district (§17-3-0207).
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone.** Any project triggering an ARO entitlement is subject to affordable unit requirements [4]. Uptown has 20 ARO projects totaling 976 affordable units in the community area.
- **Special Service Area: Greater Ravenswood SSA.** This parcel falls within the Greater Ravenswood Special Service Area, which provides supplemental services funded by a dedicated property tax levy.
- **Flood Zone X** — Area of Minimal Flood Hazard. No Special Flood Hazard Area designation; flood insurance is not required by federal mandate.
- **No PMD, no lakefront protection, no pedestrian-street overlay, no landmark district.**

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

Because this parcel is in a transit-served location (CTA and Metra TOD overlay), **the minimum parking requirement can be reduced by up to 100%** under §17-10-0102-B — meaning no off-street parking is required. This is a by-right reduction; no special entitlement is needed for the parking relief alone.

---

### 6. Height, FAR, and What Transit Does (and Doesn't) Change

- **Maximum FAR: 2.2** | **Maximum height: 45–50 ft** (§17-3-0102). On a 4,347 sq ft lot, 2.2 FAR yields a maximum of ~9,563 sq ft of floor area across all floors.
- **Parking:** Transit proximity eliminates the parking minimum by right (see #5 above).
- **Density/FAR/height bonus from transit: No.** The reduced lot-area-per-unit and density bonuses available in "dash-3" districts [4] (§17-3-0402-B) apply only to B-3 and C-3 districts, not B1-2. A density or FAR bonus here would require either a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment (§17-13-0302), a Planned Development (§17-13-0600), or an ARO entitlement — none of which is by right. Transit proximity at this district changes **parking only**, not density, FAR, or height.

---

### Confidence & What Could Not Be Determined

**Confident:** Zoning district, FAR, height, lot-area-per-unit density, parking reduction, overlay designations — all from authoritative city GIS and the zoning table.

**Could not determine from retrieved text:** Specific setback requirements, lot coverage limits, and the precise parking minimums before the 100% transit reduction (the code section §17-10-0102 was not retrieved in full). Verify these at §17-3-0500 (setbacks) and §17-10-0102 (parking schedule).

---

*This information is based on official city documents but does not constitute legal advice. Please consult a licensed attorney or contact the Department of Planning & Development for official guidance.*
